brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb (seven hexagonal cells in a honeycomb arrangement)
requirements.evidence: Seven full base cells at level 0: centre piece:0,0,0;full ringed by piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:-1,1,0;full, piece:0,-1,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full — one connected body per check_build, arranged centre-plus-six-ring.

requirements.requirement: Standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet
requirements.evidence: Three stud spikes placed facing down (variant stud, facing down per find_sockets offers s20/s23/s24): spike:0#-1,0|-1,1|0,0, spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1 and spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at three spread junctions of the honeycomb, so the seven cells rest on these feet.

requirements.requirement: House rules: open faces capped and joints locked once parts settled
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 18 solid caps on the perimeter faces; lockJoints added 12 joint bolts. check_build reports ok with no issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell honeycomb — a centre full cell ringed by six full cells at level 0 — standing on three stud spikes facing down at spread junctions as feet. Open side faces were capped with solid end caps and all joints bolted locked. Final check_build passes with no issues and meshClash clear; 40 parts total (7 bases, 3 spikes, 18 caps, 12 joint bolts). No props added, as the brief is purely structural with no use to stage.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Seven-cell honeycomb on stud-spike feet — first inspecting the current build and where bases and spikes fit.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

events.text: Starting from one cell, I'll add the six surrounding cells to make the seven-cell honeycomb.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.
